It sets itself apart from standard 3DGS by using a generative model (Shap-E) to initialize the point cloud instead of Structure from Motion (SfM), and by optimizing Gaussian parameters via 2D Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) [S1, S2].

The claim states that the method uses Shap-E to initialize the point cloud instead of Structure from Motion (SfM) and optimizes Gaussian parameters via 2D Score Distillation Sampling (SDS). Source [S1] explicitly confirms that GaussianDreamer 'utilizes Shap-E [245] to generate the initial point cloud and optimizes 3DGS using 2D SDS.' Source [S2] further corroborates the optimization mechanism, describing the paradigm where 'gradients are back-propagated through the differentiable GS renderer to update Gaussian parameters' using a 'powerful 2D or multi-view diffusion model' (which corresponds to SDS). While the evidence does not explicitly mention 'Structure from Motion' as the alternative being replaced, the context of using a generative model (Shap-E) for initialization in a text-to-3D pipeline inherently distinguishes it from traditional SfM-based initialization methods used in standard 3DGS reconstruction. Therefore, all factual components of the claim are supported by the provided evidence.
